title: Introduce model feature profiles, pricing/limits fields, and OpenAI-compat shim on model index
author: Amina Patel
description:
Motivation: Product teams need a richer, discoverable model index that lets runtime routing, SDKs, and the OpenAI-compat shim make deterministic choices about streaming/structured-output/tooling support and unit economics. This PR adds a non-breaking extension to the model listing endpoint: feature profiles, explicit compatibility flags (streaming stability, function/tool-calling, structured output), and first-class pricing/limits fields.

Summary of changes: added a new optional top-level `features` object per-model (see example below) that contains stable enumerations for capabilities; added `pricing` and `limits` objects for per-model unit economics and enforced limits; added `openai_compatibility` metadata to help the compat shim choose the closest match. Changes are additive and default to safe fallbacks so clients that ignore new fields are unaffected.

Example (excerpt of returned model list entry):
{
  "id": "redwood/fastgen-1",
  "display_name": "FastGen v1 (fp16-q4)",
  "features": ["streaming_stable", "function_calling", "structured_json_output"],
  "openai_compatibility": ["chat.completions", "functions_v1"],
  "pricing": {"tokens_per_usd_1k": "2400", "min_request_usd": "0.0005"},
  "limits": {"max_input_tokens": "8192", "max_output_tokens": "2048"}
}

Notes on compatibility: existing clients will continue to see `id`/`display_name` and older schema fields as before. The new arrays are optional; omission == conservative capability. The OpenAI-compat shim uses `openai_compatibility` to map requested OpenAI-style endpoints to the best matching Redwood model and to populate compatibility warnings when exact feature parity doesn't exist.

Implementation details: server: model-registry schema migrations (non-destructive), API layer: model index serializer extended to include computed feature profiles (derived from model metadata and runtime test results), runtime: small runtime probe that marks `streaming_stable` only after a 48h canary & n=1000 streaming traces without reordering or stalled chunks, pricing: adds a lightweight per-model ruleset to the catalog service so billing can use catalog fields as authoritative.

Testing and rollout: unit + integration tests added for API responses, e2e test that runs the openai-compat shim against the new fields, and a feature-flagged rollout to 20% of requests for one week before full enable. Canary metrics to watch: streaming rebuffer rate, function-call error rate, and reconciliation diffs between catalog pricing and billing ledger.

Migration notes for SDKs: SDKs should prefer the `features` enumeration and surface a `Model.features` accessor. OpenAI-compat shim will fall back to previous heuristics if `openai_compatibility` is absent.

Checklist:
- [x] Schema migration (catalog DB) — added nullable columns and backfilled shallow defaults
- [x] API serializer + docs updates
- [x] SDK compatibility tests (python/ts)
- [x] Runtime streaming probe and gating
- [x] Rollout plan and canary dashboard

Related: this ties into ENG-1793 (model discovery) and ENG-1810 (openai-compat improvements). For support cases the SUP-643 ticket asked for clearer guidance when a requested OpenAI feature isn't supported by the backing model.
commits_summary: 6 commits: initial schema migration + backfill; add feature extraction logic in catalog service; expose fields in model-index API; implement runtime streaming probe and gate; add pricing/limits plumbing; docs/examples + SDK notes.
review_comments: Carlos Nguyen: Left a few nits on naming (prefer 'features' enum over 'capabilities') and requested a schema doc entry for every enum value.
Amina Patel: Addressed naming nits in commit 4; added docs snippet with canonical enum definitions.
Riley Morgan: Asked for a short-circuit path in the compat shim when `openai_compatibility` lists exact mapping; added in commit 5.
Priya Shah: Verified the streaming probe doesn't add measurable latency in microbenchmarks; approved once canary gating mode was documented.
QA: Found a flaky integration test with streaming order; we fixed by increasing probe retry window and added deterministic ordering asserts.
merge_info: Merged by squash on 2025-11-12 after approvals from Carlos Nguyen and Priya Shah. Release note flagged for v2025.11.14. Changelog entry added.
release_notes: Add optional model listing fields: 'features' (enumerated capability tags), 'openai_compatibility' (list of compat targets), 'pricing' and 'limits' objects. These fields are additive and do not break existing clients. SDKs should read 'features' for capability decisions.
notes_for_ops: Rollout is feature-flagged. Enable 'catalog-feature-profiles' for 20% of traffic at first, monitor streaming_rebuffer_rate and function_call_error_rate. Backout by disabling flag and reverting canary probe activation.
post_merge_tasks: 1) Enable feature-flagged rollout; 2) Run backfill job to populate pricing defaults for legacy models; 3) Publish SDK patch for features accessor; 4) Update console filters to use features enum.
